newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to delay oil output hike of 100,000 bpd.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to delay oil output hike of 100,000 bpd.

text.p: An IMF-requested adjustment in state-run Venezuelan oil company PDVSA's investment program will affect a planned output increase by about 100,000 barrels per day (pbd), Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta said Monday.
"Some projects have had to be postponed for a couple a years therefore there'll be a delay in incorporating an additional 100,000 bpd," Arrieta told reporters at a year-end meeting.
"There are not substantial reductions, just postponements,"

The International Monetary Fund has asked PDVSA to scale back its $6.5 billion investment program for 1997 by $950 million. The IMF request forms part of a wider recommendation that Venezuela deepen fiscal reforms and lower spending to reduce inflation.
PDVSA plans to boost crude output capacity from 3.1 million bpd to over six million bpd in the next 10 years through phased investments of up to $68 billion dollars.
